newsitem.title: USA: Boeing /McDonnell vie over defense plant -WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Boeing /McDonnell vie over defense plant -WSJ.

text.p: The future role of McDonnell Douglas Corp's defense operations in St Louis has become a major source of contention, with Boeing Co's $14 billion acquisition of McDonnell all but completed, The Wall Street Journal said.
In Monday's electronic edition, The Journal said the issue has divided the senior ranks, including Phil Condit, Boeing's chairman and chief executive, and Harry Stonecipher, McDonnell Douglas's CEO.

The dispute is over the question of whether St. Louis, the headquarters for McDonnell's defense business, will become the center for all of Boeing's military-related defense and space programs, or become just a part of it, the paper said.
There is also disagreement of who should head the operations, an executive from Boewing or McDonnell, the article said.
In the past week, the paper said, the two men have turned to a former Pentagon official, Paul Kaminski, to help them resolve the dispute.
The article cites "senior executives on both sides" who say the failure to resolve the question already has begun to slow some decision-making on military contract matters.
